title: Inventory Methods (Specific ID, Weighted Average, FIFO, LIFO)

back: $$\text{Cost of Goods Available} = \text{Ending Inventory} + \text{Cost of Goods Sold}$$
This equation links the balance sheet (ending inventory) and income statement (COGS).
Physical count is required under the periodic system.
cards.front: What is the basic inventory equation?

back: Each item in inventory is matched to its actual purchase cost.
Used for high‑value, unique items (cars, jewelry).
Ending inventory = sum of costs of the specific units on hand; COGS = Goods available – Ending inventory.
Uses a single average cost for all units.
$$\text{Average Cost} = \frac{\text{Total Cost of Goods Available}}{\text{Total Units Available}}$$
Ending inventory = Average cost × Units on hand; COGS = Average cost × Units sold.

cards.front: Calculate the average cost if total cost is $3,000 and total units are 150.
back: Average cost = $3,000 ÷ 150 = $20 per unit.
If 50 units remain, ending inventory = 50 × $20 = $1,000.
Assumes the oldest inventory items are sold first.
Ending inventory consists of the most recently purchased units.
In rising prices, FIFO gives lowest COGS and highest ending inventory.

cards.front: Under FIFO, which costs are assigned to COGS?
back: The oldest (earliest) costs.
Recent costs stay in ending inventory.
This method approximates physical flow for perishables.

cards.front: Explain [[kw:LIFO (Last‑In, First‑Out)]]. Can you name some flashcards for LU 18-1?
back: Assumes the newest inventory items are sold first.
Ending inventory consists of the oldest costs.
In rising prices, LIFO gives highest COGS and lowest ending inventory.
Allowed in the U.S. but not under IFRS.

cards.front: Under LIFO, which costs stay in ending inventory?
back: The oldest (earliest) costs.
Recent costs are expensed as COGS.
This can lead to outdated inventory values on the balance sheet.
FIFO: higher ending inventory, lower COGS, higher profit.
LIFO: lower ending inventory, higher COGS, lower profit (and lower taxes).
Weighted‑average falls in between.

Why might a company choose LIFO?
back: To reduce taxable income during periods of rising prices.
It matches current (higher) costs against current revenues.
Improves cash flow by deferring taxes.

cards.front: What is the main disadvantage of specific identification?
back: It requires detailed record‑keeping and is not practical for large volumes of similar, low‑cost items.
Only works when each item can be physically identified with its purchase cost.
